lessons.title: Alphabet and sounds
lessons.shortExplanation: Dominican Kwéyòl writing uses letters familiar from French-influenced Caribbean orthographies, with sounds that learners should practise carefully.

lessons.commonMistakes: Do not assume every letter sounds exactly like English or French in every word.
lessons.practiceActivity: Say bonjou, mèsi and dlo slowly. Tap each syllable, then listen again if audio is available.
lessons.pronunciationSupport: Use the pronunciation guides on word pages while listening practice is expanded.

examples.english: a brighter vowel sound, as often taught in 'mèsi'

lessons.title: Greetings
lessons.shortExplanation: Start conversations with everyday greetings such as bonjou and bonswa.
lessons.commonMistakes: Using a morning greeting late at night can sound odd; match the greeting to the time of day when you can.
lessons.practiceActivity: Match each greeting to the best time of day, then say it aloud.
lessons.pronunciationSupport: Practise with the Adult Dictionary audio controls when files are available.

lessons.title: Sentence order
lessons.shortExplanation: Many everyday Kwéyòl sentences follow a familiar subject–marker–verb–object pattern. Learn with short model sentences first.
lessons.examplesJson: [{"kweyol":"Mwen ka manjé.","english":"I am eating."},{"kweyol":"Papa ka vini.","english":"Dad is coming."}]
lessons.commonMistakes: Translating word-for-word from English can place markers in the wrong spot.
lessons.practiceActivity: Reorder word tiles for two short sentences, then check the model answers in the practice quiz.

lessons.title: Questions and negatives
lessons.shortExplanation: Questions and negatives often rely on question words and negation markers. Learn a few high-frequency patterns before longer sentences.
lessons.examplesJson: [{"kweyol":"Kouman ou yé?","english":"How are you?"},{"kweyol":"Mwen pa konnèt.","english":"I do not know."}]
lessons.commonMistakes: Forgetting the negation marker when trying to say a negative sentence.
lessons.practiceActivity: Turn two affirmative sentences into negatives using the patterns from this lesson.
